name: Neistra v0.26.2 — Application-owned viewer interface
body:
Neistra owns the viewer controls and feedback around the existing molecular canvas. Native controls, hover-information text, toast/task overlays and branding are removed. **Existing orientation axes remain**, as explicitly requested.

Implemented under the [approved #96 contract](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/blob/master/docs/plans/issue-96-application-owned-viewer.md) in [PR #129](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/pull/129), normally merged with checkpoint history preserved. Exact qualified runtime: `e1cae49a9655a4a48a72c25f36bbd45db0273423`.

## Highlights and fixes

- Existing Neistra camera, selection, style, measurement, surface, editing and job controls remain the supported interface. Molecular labels, measurements, interaction markers, hover highlighting and previews retain the existing renderer and canonical state owners.
- Loading feedback spans actual scene synchronization. Obsolete completion/errors cannot replace the active viewer's feedback. Scientific/import warnings and actionable job/surface/minimization errors remain visible.
- Failed/late mounts clean up. Canvas teardown finishes outside the parent React commit before plugin disposal. Projection-only camera jitter no longer cancels native double-click expansion; physical camera and canonical membership behavior remain intact.
- Obsolete native CSS/DOM observers and popup-clearance code are removed. The complete byte-identical Mol* license ships at `/licenses/molstar.txt`, with repository attribution in `docs/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Persisted data, migrations and compatibility

Stable patch **0.26.2** corrects presentation and interaction reliability without adding scientific capabilities or changing public contracts. All five authoritative version sources agree. This release includes the previously unreleased 0.26.1 changes after published v0.26.0; no separate 0.26.1 release is required.

No dependency upgrade, database migration, HTTP/job/plugin contract or scientific-model change. Alembic **0014**, project/viewer/archive **2**, and normalized/selection/component **1** remain. Original uploads, molecular coordinates, selections, scenes, surfaces, history and jobs retain their contracts. Archives continue to retain current state; Undo history remains in the managed store.

Actual tagged v0.26.0 and final v0.26.2 producer/readers pass both directions, with explicit implementation-root/version checks and retained originals/coordinates, batch history, saved selections/scenes/surfaces, jobs and archive remapping. Upgrade normally with matching application components and complete managed-store backups. Compatible rollback requires no data stripping or schema downgrade.

## Inherited unreleased changes

PR #126 supplies Carbon only as the initial coloring mode and remembers explicit choices for the application runtime across panels/projects/remounts, resetting on reload. D-148 separates mandatory portable correctness from additional strict reference-host timing with `NEISTRA_PERFORMANCE=1`. Scientific policies, production deadlines, resource bounds and dependency locks remain unchanged.

## Verification

Both the clean candidate (`117c35480586edffc2bb1cc72a06df934e0b59b8`) and exact merged master (`e1cae49a9655a4a48a72c25f36bbd45db0273423`) pass all **20 release commands**: **1,262 Python tests (zero skips), 374 frontend, 12 supervisor/policy and 352 browser tests**, with **62 exactly unchanged layout exclusions**, zero failures/flakes/automatic retries. All **595 source identities** match across candidate and master; lossless log hashes verify. Both actual tagged-reader directions pass on each gate. Frozen installs, fresh migration, Ruff/mypy, frontend lint/types/build, version/dependency/schema and shipped-license audits pass. Both themes/layouts, actual 100%/200% zoom, native picking/surfaces/previews, exact state/original/camera invariants and annotation/task/remount/project workflows are covered. Four native projection-jitter records verify two real updates/events with equal physical camera snapshots and exact expansion. Portable correctness is qualified; strict reference-host timing is not claimed.

Earlier failed/interrupted attempts, fail-first regressions and corrections remain in the evidence. They are not substituted for the final clean gates. The qualification ZIP contains raw browser reports, retained screenshots/traces, native scientific evidence, actual-reader records, exact commands/environment, source/log identities and an internal SHA-256 manifest.

Complete local full-diff review is implementer self-review. [Codex review was requested](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/pull/129#issuecomment-6592134908) and verified remotely; no external review result or finding returned before publication. No independent approval is claimed. No required human approval or unresolved review conversation was bypassed.

## Deliberately simplified, deferred or rejected

Native screenshot/settings entry points disappear deliberately. [#128](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/issues/128) separately scopes Neistra-owned molecular image export (content, dimensions/background, annotations and download semantics). This nonblocking follow-up is not an unfinished essential #96 outcome.

Automatic parity with every native function is rejected as unnecessary scope. No new hover-information overlay, generic task mirror, fullscreen/XR/illumination/animation panel, snapshot format or renderer upgrade is introduced. Existing selection inspection and application feedback remain. Detached presentation [#97](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/issues/97), warning inspection [#98](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/issues/98) and renderer-patch maintenance [#107](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/issues/107) remain independent.

## Known limitations

Existing scientific interpretation, browser/rendering and capacity limits remain. Annotation placement/overlap is unchanged; this release adds no label collision avoidance or measurement algorithm. The renderer stays pinned with its existing pick-readback patch. Portable qualification measures timings but does not qualify strict reference-host throughput or claim a performance improvement.

Qualification asset: `neistra-v0.26.2-qualification.zip` (124,988,688 bytes; 1,304 entries). SHA-256: `6ae3fc4558626a4272c1afed402f6fd7170ce3fcb48964928420fab40d99cf76`. The complete Mol* notice and third-party attribution accompany the evidence.
